Implementation and traceability: - Rule implementation: src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - JSDoc ties directly to this story and requirements: - `@story docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md` - `@req REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE`, `REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION`, `REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION`, `REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY`, `REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS`, `REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION`, `REQ-ERROR-HANDLING`. - Uses `const cwd = (context as any).cwd ?? process.cwd();` for path resolution (matches Implementation Notes about preferring context.cwd). - Parses annotations (REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION): - `handleComment` splits comment text into lines, normalizes them, and finds lines starting with `@story`. - `validateStoryPath` splits the line by whitespace and extracts the file path token, then calls `processStoryPath`. - Core validation flow: - Security: `performSecurityValidations` blocks disallowed absolute paths and unsafe traversal before further checks (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). - Extension: if `requireExt` is true and `hasValidExtension(storyPath)` is false, reports `invalidExtension` with the offending `path` (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE). - Existence: `reportExistenceProblems` calls `normalizeStoryPath` (from utils) to compute candidates + existence result, delegates boundary logic to `handleProjectBoundaryForExistence`, and then calls `reportExistenceStatus` to emit `fileMissing` or `fileAccessError` (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING). - Messages (User Experience): - `fileMissing: "Story file '{{path}}' not found"`. - `invalidExtension: "Invalid story file extension for '{{path}}', expected '.story.md'"`. - `invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{path}}'"`. - `fileAccessError: "Could not validate story file '{{path}}' due to a filesystem error: {{error}}. Please check file existence and permissions."`. - These clearly identify which path failed and why, satisfying the UX and error-handling criteria. - Rule meta schema: - Options object with `storyDirectories: string[]`, `allowAbsolutePaths: boolean`, `requireStoryExtension: boolean` (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS).
- Supporting utilities: src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts - Annotated with story 006.0 and requirements including REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY. - Path resolution (REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION): - `buildStoryCandidates(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs)` builds absolute candidate paths: - If storyPath starts with `./` or `../`, resolves directly against cwd. - Otherwise, first resolves `cwd + storyPath`, then `cwd + dir + basename(storyPath)` for each configured story directory. - Existence and caching (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION): - `fileExistStatusCache: Map` caches filesystem results. - `checkSingleCandidate` wraps `fs.existsSync` and `fs.statSync` in try/catch: - Non-existent paths => `{status: 'missing'}`. - Existing regular files => `{status: 'exists'}`. - Non-file entries => `{status: 'missing'}`. - Any fs error => `{status: 'fs-error', error}` (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING). - `getStoryExistence` returns first `exists` match; if none, prefers first `fs-error`; otherwise returns `missing`. - `storyExists(paths)` returns `true` only when status is `exists`. - `normalizeStoryPath(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs)` returns `{candidates, exists, existence}` combining candidates and aggregated existence. - `__resetStoryExistenceCacheForTests` allows resetting cache between tests (used in tests). - Security & boundaries: - `enforceProjectBoundary(candidate, cwd)` computes `isWithinProject` by comparing resolved paths, implementing REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY. - Helpers `isAbsolutePath`, `containsPathTraversal`, `isTraversalUnsafe`, `hasValidExtension`, `isUnsafeStoryPath` support REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION.
- Boundary/security helpers: src/rules/helpers/valid-story-reference-helpers.ts - File-level JSDoc references story 006.0 and REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS. - `analyzeCandidateBoundaries(candidates, cwd)` iterates over candidates, calling `enforceProjectBoundary`, tracking whether any candidates are in-project vs out-of-project (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - `handleProjectBoundaryForExistence` implements core project boundary logic: - If `candidates` non-empty, and there are out-of-project candidates but no in-project candidates, it calls `reportInvalidPath` and returns true (rejects paths entirely outside project, even if they exist). - If `existenceResult.status === 'exists'` but the matched path is outside the boundary, it also calls `reportInvalidPath` and returns true. - Otherwise returns false so standard existence/error reporting can proceed. - `performSecurityValidations`: - When path is absolute and `allowAbsolute` is false, reports `invalidPath` and stops further processing (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - For traversal-like patterns, resolves the normalized absolute path and reports `invalidPath` if it escapes cwd (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY).

`[REQ-EXTENSION] valid .story.md extension`. - `[REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION] valid relative path with ./ prefix`. - Invalid tests exercising core behavior and messaging: - Missing file: expects `fileMissing` with correct `data.path`. - Wrong extension: expects `invalidExtension` with `data.path`. - Path traversal: expects `invalidPath`. - Absolute path not allowed: expects `invalidPath`. - Additional targeted RuleTester instances: - `configurablePathsTester` verifies custom `storyDirectories` resolution. - `allowAbsolutePathsTester` verifies `allowAbsolutePaths` true/false behavior, including invalidPath when disallowed. - `relaxedExtensionTester` verifies `requireStoryExtension: false` allows `.story.md` and (via later Jest helper tests) `.md`. - `projectBoundaryTester` asserts story reference outside project root (via absolute path to `/outside-project/...`) is rejected with `invalidPath` when storyDirectories point outside the project (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - Jest-based configuration/boundary tests: - Block `describe("Valid Story Reference Rule Configuration and Boundaries (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)", ...)`: - Uses `runRuleOnCode` to run rule directly, verifying that diagnostics arrays are produced and no crashes occur. - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] uses storyDirectories when resolving relative paths` – uses `mockFsForExistingFile` to simulate presence of a story file and ensures resolution works. - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] allowAbsolutePaths permits absolute paths inside project when enabled` – verifies no error when absolute in-project path is allowed. - `[REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY] storyDirectories cannot escape project even when normalize resolves outside cwd` – ensures diagnostics are produced when a traversal path is used. - `[REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY] misconfigured storyDirectories outside project cannot validate external files` – mocks an external file under a temp outside dir and asserts at least one `invalidPath` diagnostic. - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] requireStoryExtension=false accepts existing .md story file` – mocks `docs/stories/developer-story.map.md`, runs with `requireStoryExtension: false`, and asserts zero `invalidExtension` diagnostics. - Error-handling tests (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING): - `describe("Valid Story Reference Rule Error Handling (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)", ...)`: - `storyExists returns false when fs throws` – mocks `fs.existsSync` and `fs.statSync` to throw `EACCES`, validates no exception and boolean false. - `storyExists returns false when fs.statSync throws EIO and existsSync is true` – simulates stat I/O error and validates behavior. - `rule reports fileAccessError when fs.statSync throws and existsSync is true` – expects at least one diagnostic with `messageId: 'fileAccessError'` and error text containing `EIO`. - `rule reports fileAccessError when fs throws` – mocks both fs calls to throw `EACCES`, expects `fileAccessError` diagnostics and error text containing `EACCES`.

traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION are implemented and verified. Core functionality is provided by the `valid-story-reference` ESLint rule, which validates that @story annotations reference existing .story.md files, enforces the correct extension, and uses configurable story directories and cwd-based path resolution. Quality and safety requirements are met via dedicated utilities that wrap filesystem operations in try/catch, cache existence checks for performance, and enforce project boundaries and security (no traversal or disallowed absolute paths). Error messages clearly distinguish between missing files, invalid extensions, invalid paths, and filesystem access errors, and tests assert both the presence and content of these diagnostics. Integration with prior annotation validation is evident by relying on parsed @story lines and working alongside the other traceability rules. Documentation in docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md explains behavior, configuration, boundary semantics, and examples consistent with the story’s Implementation Notes. All related Jest tests for this story, its helpers, and error handling pass in the recorded test run, so the story is fully satisfied.
